title: Surveillance Cameras / ALPR Systems (Flock Safety) – Town of Fishkill

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: FOIL Request – Surveillance Cameras / ALPR Systems (Flock Safety) – Town of Fishkill
communications.communication:
Dear Records Custodian,

Under the provisions of the New York Freedom of Information Law (FOIL), N.Y. Public Officers Law §§ 84–90, I hereby request access to and copies of records held by the Town of Fishkill, Dutchess County, relating to the planning, proposal, procurement, authorization, or attempted deployment of Flock Safety surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems.

This request is made in the public interest to better understand the use, consideration, or implementation of surveillance technologies by local government entities, including decision-making processes, vendor relationships, and potential impacts on public privacy.

The purpose of this request is to determine the origin, authorization process, procurement activity, proposed locations, and communications surrounding any surveillance camera system, including identifying which individual, agency, or vendor first initiated discussions or planning for such a program within the Town of Fishkill.

Timeframe: January 1, 2023 – Present, including any earlier records referencing or relating to Flock Safety, automated license plate readers, or surveillance cameras within the Town of Fishkill.

Records Requested

For the purpose of this request, the records I seek include, but are not limited to the following:

1. Contracts and Agreements

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, vendor agreements, procurement documents, or proposals involving the Town of Fishkill and Flock Safety or any related entities concerning surveillance cameras, automated license plate readers, or related monitoring technology.

This includes draft contracts, executed agreements, amendments, pilot program agreements, trial program documentation, cancellation notices, procurement justifications, and contract termination records.

Legal Basis: Contracts involving public funds or public infrastructure are public records subject to disclosure under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87.

2. Records Identifying Project Initiation

All records reflecting the initial introduction, proposal, solicitation, or outreach regarding Flock Safety cameras or ALPR systems, including records identifying:

• the individual or office that first proposed or recommended the system  
• the first communications between the Town and Flock Safety  
• vendor outreach to town officials  
• internal discussions about introducing the technology  
• marketing or sales outreach from vendors  

3. Internal Communications

All internal communications including emails, memoranda, text messages, chat messages, letters, meeting notes, or other correspondence among:

• the Town Supervisor  
• Town Board members  
• Town of Fishkill Police Department personnel  
• Town administrative staff  
• Town legal counsel  
• Highway or Building Department personnel  
• other municipal offices  

that discuss:

• Flock Safety  
• automated license plate readers  
• surveillance cameras  
• camera deployments  
• vendor procurement or negotiations  
• surveillance technology adoption  

4. Communications With External Entities

All communications between the Town of Fishkill and:

• representatives of Flock Safety  
• technology vendors or consultants  
• Dutchess County officials  
• local, state, or federal law enforcement agencies  
• regional intelligence or real-time crime centers  

concerning surveillance cameras, ALPR systems, or the Flock Safety program.

5. Vendor Demonstrations and Sales Outreach

All records relating to vendor presentations, product demonstrations, marketing materials, or sales outreach regarding Flock Safety or related surveillance technology, including:

• presentation decks  
• vendor proposals  
• demonstration scheduling emails  
• meeting invitations or call summaries  
• webinar invitations  
• follow-up communications  

6. Proposed Camera Locations and Site Selection

All records identifying, evaluating, or discussing proposed or potential locations for surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader systems within the Town of Fishkill.

This includes but is not limited to:

• maps showing proposed camera placements  
• GIS maps or infrastructure maps  
• deployment plans  
• proposed installation locations or intersections  
• roadway monitoring points  
• entry or exit routes to the town  
• communications discussing site selection  
• vendor recommendations for placement  
• field surveys or site inspections  
• infrastructure or engineering assessments related to camera placement  

7. Deployment and Planning Documents

All planning or operational records relating to the surveillance system, including:

• deployment plans  
• camera location maps  
• infrastructure assessments  
• equipment specifications  
• installation schedules  
• operational capability descriptions  
• technology architecture documents  

8. Financial and Procurement Records

All records relating to funding, budgeting, or procurement of the surveillance system, including:

• invoices  
• payment records  
• purchase authorizations  
• budget allocations  
• grant applications  
• cost analyses  
• procurement justifications  
• financial approvals  

9. Meeting Records

All agendas, minutes, recordings, transcripts, or notes from Town Board meetings, committee meetings, departmental meetings, or internal meetings where surveillance camera programs or Flock Safety systems were discussed, proposed, approved, or canceled.

10. Oversight, Audit, and Compliance Records

Any audit reports, legal opinions, compliance reviews, investigations, or internal analyses relating to surveillance camera programs or procurement processes.

11. Data Access, Sharing, and Integration

All records relating to data access or sharing involving the surveillance system, including:

• agreements allowing other agencies to access camera data  
• policies governing license plate reader searches  
• records concerning integration with regional surveillance networks  
• data retention policies  
• privacy or civil liberties assessments  

Electronic Records and Metadata

For all responsive electronic records, including emails and digital documents, I request that records be produced in their native electronic format where possible, including all available metadata and email header information.

This includes, but is not limited to:

• sender and recipient information  
• CC and BCC fields  
• full email header routing data  
• timestamps for sending and receipt  
• message ID fields  
• attachment metadata  
• document creation dates  
• last modified dates  
• author fields  
• file path information where available  

Providing metadata is necessary to determine the origin, timing, and authorship of communications relating to the surveillance camera proposal.

Request for Segregable Non-Exempt Portions

Should any portion of the requested records be deemed exempt from disclosure, I request the release of any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions in accordance with N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87(2).

Preservation of Records

Please note your obligation not to destroy or alter any records potentially responsive to this request. Once a FOIL request has been received, agencies are required to preserve all responsive records during processing.

Fee Waiver Request

I request a fee waiver for the processing of this request as the information sought is in the public interest and its disclosure will contribute significantly to public understanding of government surveillance programs and decision-making processes.

If potential fees exceed $200, please inform me before proceeding.

Public Availability of Communications

Please be advised that communications relating to this request, including incoming and outgoing correspondence, may be publicly published on transparency platforms such as MuckRock.com.

Statutory Response Time

As required under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 89(3), I look forward to acknowledgment of this request within five business days.

Sincerely,

Jordan Lassiter  
Independent Investigative Journalist

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Somerville Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Somerville Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Dakota County, MN - LexisNexis / AVCC Audit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

A previous public records requested showed that DCSO is sharing CAD & RMS data with LexisNexis for inclusion in their Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) product. This request seeks to better understand who has access to that data once it's been copied to the data broker, and how it is used. To that end, we are requesting the following records:

1) Signed/Executed "AVCC XML Addendum" (sometimes just "XML Addendum" or similar). This includes the clause that dictates how LexisNexis may share DCSO's local data. An example may be found here: https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28549832-san-luis-obispo-avcc-addendum/?mode=document#document/p1/a2826398

2) Audit logs from AVCC of outside agencies querying DCSO data. Typically this is only accessible to AVCC/ACA administrators. From our understanding, the system only keeps 30 or 90 days of records, however if a longer audit log timeframe is available, we'd like to request audit logs from 12/1/2025 through present. Please include the agency who searched/accessed DCSO data, and any reason code or information they may have included.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident location, area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

All Office of Children and Family Services data and documents that the Office of the State Comptroller used to research the following paragraph: "OCFS’ incident data shows an increase in certain types of incidents between January 1, 2019 and December 31, 2022. For example, in secure facilities, there were no incidents relating to controlled substance contraband in 2019; however, in 2022, there were 37 incidents. Positive urine drug screenings were also up overall, by about 24% for the same period. Further, instances of self-harm at secure facilities were up 100% (from 24 to 48 incidents) – and those that included an expression or gesture of suicide were up 667% (from three to 23 incidents)."

That paragraph can be found on page 13 of OSC report 2022-S-13. The link to that report is here: https://www.osc.ny.gov/files/state-agencies/audits/pdf/sga-2024-22s13.pdf

Please note that FOIL §87(2)(g) (the "inter-agency or intra-agency materials" exemption) does not apply to this request as that exemption does not apply to "statistical or factual tabulations or data."

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

title: Sheriff data collection (2017-2022) (Racine County Sheriff's Office)

communications.subject: Wisconsin Open Records Act Request: Sheriff data collection (2017-2022) (Racine County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. the total number of use of force incidents from 2017-2022, separated by year. Please include as part of this a breakdown of how many use of force incidents in 2022 were related to law enforcement operations and how many were related to correctional/custodial operations. 
2. the total number of use of force incidents, separated by year and type of force, from 2017-2022 (for example, information that specifies the number of taser incidents in 2022, baton incidents in 2022, etc.)
3. the total number of civilian complaints against law enforcement that were reported and the total number sustained from 2017-2022, separated by year.  
4. the total number of civilian complaints alleging law enforcement use of excessive force that were reported and the total number sustained from 2017-2022, separated by year. 
5. the total number of civilian complaints alleging biased policing or racial profiling that were reported and the total number sustained from 2017-2022, separated by year.  
6. the total number of civilian complaints alleging criminal conduct that were reported and the total number sustained from 2017-2022, separated by year. 
7. the total number of officer-involved shootings from 2017-2022, both fatal and non-fatal, separated by year.
8. the total number of people who the sheriff’s department used force against, broken down by race/ethnicity, in 2022.

When available, I would appreciate being sent individualized data for each item in this request in spreadsheet format. If individualized data are unavailable, please send information that includes aggregate statistics for the item instead.  

Note that my requests for civilian complaints are specifically for civilian complaints alleging police misconduct, please do not include complaints filed by one officer/the department against another officer.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Samuel Sinyangwe

conducting nine days of early voting, the rolling canvass, the post-election
canvass, completing all required audits, and the ultimate certification of the
election results. Further, the Board is completing its required activities to
prepare for the 2026 Primary and General Elections, including the
imminent filing period for election documents, corresponding cures,
objections, and subsequent ballot access hearings for the June 2026 Primary
Election. This important statutory function of the Board requires the full
attention of staff to fulfill the Board's legal mandates regarding the

misdemeanor (NYS Election Law § 17-168).

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Tisbury Police)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Tisbury Police)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

1. The current records control schedule(s), records disposition schedule(s), and file plan(s) governing records created or maintained by the OPPT Biotechnology Program, including any schedules approved by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA).
2. Any internal guidance, indexes, or documents that identify the categories of records the Biotechnology Program creates or maintains in connection with submissions for microorganisms under TSCA Section 5 — including but not limited to TSCA Experimental Release Applications (TERAs), Microbial Commercial Activity Notices (MCANs), Tier I exemption notices, and Tier II exemption notices.
3. Any records retention or disposal forms (e.g., SF-115 or equivalent) submitted to NARA in the last five years that cover Biotechnology Program records.

Date range: I am requesting current/active schedules and any versions in effect during the past five years.
Format: Electronic copies in their original format (PDF, Word, Excel) are preferred. Please provide records on a rolling basis as they become available rather than waiting for the entire request to be processed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Niko McCarty

title: 2026 code violations

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2026 code violations
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I request copies of public records concerning municipal code-enforcement actions within the City of Edmond.

Specifically, I request a digital copy, spreadsheet, or log of all residential code-enforcement violations, citations, and notices issued from January 1, 2026, through the date this request is processed.

To limit clerical search time, please provide the information in its existing electronic format, such as Excel, CSV, or a text file. I am requesting only the following fields:

- Property owner’s or responsible party’s name
- Street address
- Violation type
- Date the violation was recorded or notice was issued

If the City does not maintain a centralized spreadsheet or log containing these fields, please provide the existing underlying electronic records from which this information can be extracted.

If any responsive record does not contain the property owner’s or responsible party’s name, please provide the remaining requested fields rather than withholding the entire record.

If the estimated cost will exceed $25, please provide an itemized estimate before processing the request. I request that any fees be waived because the records will be made available to the general public and concern the enforcement of municipal health, safety, and property-maintenance laws.

If any portion of this request is denied, withheld, or redacted, please identify the specific statutory exemption under the Oklahoma Open Records Act supporting that decision and release all reasonably segregable portions of the records.

Thank you for your attention and cooperation.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

Dear Mr. Craven,

This is the Initial Agency Decision to your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the Office of the Secretary, U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs (OSVA) dated and received February 16, 2026, and assigned FOIA tracking number 26-12155-F. You requested:

All email communications between VA and White House officials between May 9, 2025 and and [sic] present day re: Executive Order 14296
(https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/05/keeping-promises-to-veterans-and-establishing-a-national-center-for-warrior-independence/)
Key words may include, but are not limited to, "NDA," "National Center for Warrior
Independence," "Los Angeles," "LA," and "tiny homes." Also please include any non disclosure agreements signed as part of efforts to execute the order.

Media Fee Category

We placed you in the media fee category. For this FOIA request, we do not charge FOIA fees. However, VA reserves the right to charge FOIA fees for future FOIA requests.

2/18/26 Microsoft 365 Search

              OSVA has conducted the below search.

Search - February 18, 2026
By: Office of Information & Technology (OI&T)
Information System: Microsoft 365 (Emails, Outlook, and Teams)
Timeframe: 5/9/25 to 2/18/26
Custodians: Doug Collins, Paul Lawrence, Chris Syrek, Lavin Gartland
Search terms: 1) 14296, NDA, "National Center for Warrior Independence," "Los Angeles," LA, or "tiny homes" AND 2) To/From: eop.gov
* Search yielded 468 pages

Initial Agency Decision

              OSVA withholds the entire four hundred sixty-eight (468) pages, Bates-numbered 1-468 in full per FOIA Exemptions 5, 6, 7(C), 7(E). Exemption 5 protects interagency or intra-agency memorandums or letters that would not be available by law to a party other than an agency in litigation with the agency, as well as civil litigation privileges. Under FOIA Exemption 5 and the presidential communications privilege, VA withholds communications and reports between the VA and the Office of the President. The presidential communications privilege protects agency communications and documents to or from the President or his advisers. Loving v. DOD, 550 F.3d 32, 37-38 (D.C. Cir. 2008) (Exemption 5 "incorporates" Presidential Communications Privilege, which protects "'communications directly involving and documents actually viewed by the President,' as well as documents 'solicited and received' by the President or his 'immediate White House advisers'" (internal citations omitted); Berman v. CIA, 378 F. Supp. 2d 1209, 1219-20 (E.D. Cal. 2005) (same), aff'd on other grounds, 501 F.3d 1136 (9th Cir. 2007); Judicial Watch, Inc. v. DOJ, 365 F.3d 1108, 1110 n.1 (D.C. Cir. 2004) ("embrac[ing] the definitional analysis set forth" in In re Sealed Case, 121 F.3d 729, 749-50, 752 (D.C. Cir. 1997), protecting documents covered by Presidential Communications Privilege); Amnesty Int'l USA v. CIA, 728 F. Supp. 2d 479, 522 (S.D.N.Y. 2010) ("all twenty documents reflect or memorialize communications between senior presidential advisers and other United States government officials and are therefore properly withheld").

Assistant Attorney General T. Elliot Gaiser, of Office of Legal Counsel, opined, "presidential communications with private advisers can fall within the scope of executive privilege so long as they relate to official presidential decisionmaking, involve or reflect communications with the President or his direct advisers, and are confidential." Applicability of Executive Privilege to Presidential Communications with Private Advisers, 50 Op. O.L.C. __ at 21 (Aug. 10, 2026), available at https://www.justice.gov/olc/media/1457271/dl. As such, VA withholds the entire requested 468 pages in full.

FOIA Exemption 5 permits an agency to withhold material reflecting the thoughts, opinions, and recommendations of federal officials reviewing an issue. Under the deliberative process privilege and FOIA Exemption 5, OSVA withholds internal government deliberations, thoughts, opinions, recommendations, and proposed solutions from federal employees reviewing VA programs in their professional capacities, as well as draft documents and briefings. The information contained in the responsive records is both predecisional and deliberative because it reflects preliminary opinions, proposed solutions, and recommendations, which do not reflect VA's final decision. Exposure of premature discussions before a final decision is made could create undue public confusion. The release of the redacted information would negatively impact the ability of federal employees to openly and frankly consider issues amongst themselves when deliberating, discussing, reviewing, proposing changes to, and making recommendations on VA programs; as well as preparing draft documents and briefings. The information reveals the thoughts, deliberations, and opinions that, if released, would have a chilling effect on the ability of federal officials and consultants to discuss, opine, recommend or be forthcoming about the agency's issues which require full and frank assessment. Here, the disclosure of the withheld information is likely to compromise the integrity of this deliberative or decision-making process. Moreover, the predecisional character of a document is not altered by the passage of time. U.S. Fish & Wildlife Serv. v. Sierra Club, Inc., 592 U.S. __, 141 S. Ct. 777, at *1 (Mar. 4, 2021) ("the privilege protects in-house drafts that proved to be the agencies' last word about a proposal's potential threat to endangered species. We hold that it does."); St. Louis Sewer Dist., No. 10-2103, at *18 (E.D. Mo. Mar. 2, 2012) (protecting e-mail communications, "press releases, talking points and 'Q & A,'" drafts, and briefing materials); Citizens for Responsibility & Ethics in Wash. v. DHS, 514 F. Supp. 2d 36, 44 (D.D.C. 2007) (protecting briefing materials concerning Hurricane Katrina response including proposed "solutions and approaches"); Judicial Watch, Inc. v. DOE, 310 F. Supp. 2d 271, 317 (D.D.C. 2004) (protecting briefing materials for Secretary of the Interior), aff'd in part, rev'd in part on other grounds & remanded, 412 F.3d 125, 133 (D.C. Cir. 2005); Klunzinger v. IRS, 27 F. Supp. 2d 1015, 1026 (W.D. 1998) (protecting paper to brief commissioner for meeting); Thompson v. Dep't of the Navy, No. 95-347, 1997 WL 527344, at *4 (D.D.C. Aug. 18, 1997) (protecting materials to brief senior officials responding to media inquiries, as "disclosure of materials reflecting the process by which the Navy formulates its policy concerning statements to and interactions with the press" could stifle frank communication within the agency), aff'd, No. 97-5292, 1998 WL 202253, at *1 (D.C. Cir. Mar. 11, 1998) (per curiam); Williams v. DOJ, 556 F. Supp. 63, 65 (D.D.C. 1982) (protecting "briefing papers prepared for the Attorney General prior to an appearance before a congressional committee").

Under FOIA Exemption 5, the attorney-client, and work product privileges, the VA withholds portions of records, emails, and communications between VA employees and attorneys relating to federal lawsuits against and legal issues concerning the VA. The release of this information would impede the ability of VA employees and attorneys to speak openly and frankly about legal issues concerning and lawsuits against the VA. The release of this information would also compromise the VA's legal positions for its current or potential lawsuits.

5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(6) exempts from required disclosure "personnel and medical files and similar files the disclosure of which would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy." FOIA Exemption 6 permits VA to withhold a document or information within a document if disclosure of the information, either by itself or in conjunction with other information available to either the public or the FOIA requester, would result in an unwarranted invasion of an individual's personal privacy without contributing significantly to the public's understanding of the activities of the federal government. Specifically, the information being withheld, as indicated on the enclosed documents, under FOIA Exemption 6, consists of names, identities, job titles, office names, email addresses, phone numbers, facsimile numbers, and meeting links and numbers and passcodes of federal employees. However, we release the names and VA contact information of VA Senior Executives. Federal employees retain a significant privacy interest under certain circumstances, such as in instances where the release of their information could represent a threat to their well-being, harassment, or their ability to function within their sphere of employment. The federal employees whose information is at issue have a substantial privacy interest in their personal information. In weighing the private versus the public interest, we find that there is no public interest in knowing this information. The coverage of FOIA Exemption 6 is absolute unless the FOIA requester can demonstrate a countervailing public interest in the requested information by demonstrating that the FOIA requester is in a position to provide the requested information to members of the general public and that the information requested contributes significantly to the public's understanding of the activities of the Federal government. Additionally, the requester must demonstrate how the public's need to understand the information significantly outweighs the privacy interest of the person to whom the information pertains. Upon consideration of the records, I have not been able to identify a countervailing public interest of sufficient magnitude to outweigh the privacy interest of the individuals whose names are redacted. The protected information has been redacted and (b)(6) inserted. "Withholding a telephone number or e-mail address, alone, is not sufficient to protect that [privacy] interest; alternate means of contacting and harassing these employees would be readily discoverable on the Internet if this court ordered their names disclosed." Long v. Immigration & Customs Enf't, 2017 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 160719 (D.C. Cir. 2017).

5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(7)(C) exempts from required disclosure information law enforcement information the disclosure of which "could reasonably be expected to constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy." Redacted information includes personal details in White House security systems and links to such. The release of this information would risk impersonation, targeting, intrusion, or violence against the health and safety of: White House employees with security clearances, U.S. Secret Service agents, VA police officers, VA employees, other federal employees, and other security details.

5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(7)(E) exempts from required disclosure information that "would disclose techniques and procedures for law enforcement investigations or prosecutions, or would disclose guidelines for law enforcement investigations or prosecutions if such disclosure could reasonably be expected to risk circumvention of the law." Redacted information includes personal details in White House security systems and links to such. The release of this information would risk impersonation, targeting, intrusion, or violence against the health and safety of: White House employees with security clearances, U.S. Secret Service agents, VA police officers, VA employees, other federal employees, and other security details. Prechtel v. FCC, 330 F. Supp. 3d 320, 335 (D.D.C. 2018) (protecting agency's electronic server logs because disclosure "would reveal sensitive information regarding [its] IT architecture, including security measures [it] takes to protect its systems from malicious activity" and would provide a "'"roadmap"'" to circumvent agency's defensive efforts (quoting agency declaration)); Poitras v. DHS, 303 F. Supp. 3d 136, 159 (D.D.C. 2018) (withholding "'protected internal e-mail addresses, non-public intranet web addresses, and a secure internal e-mail tool'" because disclosure would increase risk of unauthorized access to agency's IT system (quoting agency declaration)); Levinthal v FEC, 219 F. Supp. 3d 1, 8-9 (D.D.C. 2016) (protecting study that assesses vulnerabilities in information technology system because possible security risk exists and disclosure could permit unlawful access to agency system).

FOIA Mediation

Under the provisions of the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, the following contact information is provided to assist FOIA requesters in resolving disputes:
VA Central Office FOIA Public Liaison:
Email Address: vacofoiaservice@va.gov<mailto:vacofoiaservice@va.gov>

This concludes OSVA's Initial Agency Decision to request 26-12155-F. Please be advised that should you desire to do so, you may appeal the determination made in this response to:

of the date of this letter.

title: CPRA request — aggregate California surrogacy birth data and related data documentation

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CPRA request — aggregate California surrogacy birth data and related data documentation
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Government Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request the following records concerning live births occurring in California from January 1, 2015, through the most recent available records as of the date of this request.

This request seeks aggregate, de-identified statistical information and related data documentation. I am not requesting names, individual birth certificates, court orders, or other personally identifying information. Please include responsive information maintained in birth-registration, vital-statistics, and related registration or amendment processing systems.

**1. Annual surrogacy birth counts**

For each birth year and county of birth, the number of live-born children whose records identify a surrogacy or gestational-carrier arrangement, including parentage established by a judgment under Family Code § 7962.

Please use any maintained surrogacy indicators, registration or processing codes, or relevant notations. These include, where available, the AVSS “SURR” variable documented in the June 23, 2016 AVSS Variables/Definitions, “Surrogate Birth” comments described in CDPH’s January 2016 registration handbook, and equivalent fields in successor systems.

Include qualifying original registrations and amended or replacement records, counting each child once.

If surrogacy births cannot be separately identified, please provide, as a separately labeled fallback, annual counts by county of births registered or amended pursuant to a pre-birth or post-birth court order establishing parentage. Please distinguish available order or processing categories and identify the criteria used for each table.

**2. Parents’ countries of birth**

For the births identified under item 1, annual statewide counts by the recorded country of birth of each legal or intended parent listed on the birth certificate, with the parent fields reported separately.

Please identify the fields used and whether they describe the listed legal or intended parents, genetic parents, or gestational carrier. Include unknown or unrecorded categories where available. Keep any broader parentage-order fallback population separately labeled.

**3. Repeated parentage across births**

Annual aggregate counts of:

- Distinct individual parents listed on three or more qualifying children’s birth records within any rolling 12-month period;
- Distinct parent pairs meeting that threshold; and
- The total number of distinct qualifying children associated with those parents or parent pairs, reported separately for each measure.

Counts by calendar year are acceptable if rolling 12-month counts are not available through ordinary database extraction. Please identify the counting period and year-assignment method used.

Apply the threshold statewide, including births occurring in different California counties. Please provide statewide annual totals and county-of-birth breakdowns where available. If existing data permit, also provide the number of separate deliveries represented, so multiple children from one delivery can be distinguished from children born in separate deliveries.

If exact figures cannot be released, I am willing to accept counts of distinct individual parents and, separately, parent pairs grouped into bands of 3–5, 6–10, and 11 or more qualifying children within the applicable counting period. Statewide reporting, merging bands, and suppression of exact child totals within bands are acceptable where necessary to satisfy disclosure requirements.

If this item requires additional record linkage or custom analytical work, please advise me of the work and estimated cost before proceeding. Please continue processing the remaining items independently.

**4. Data definitions and coding documentation**

Please provide the relevant portions of existing data dictionaries, field definitions, code lists, and registration or amendment instructions describing:

- Surrogacy and gestational-carrier indicators, including AVSS “SURR,” “Surrogate Birth” comments, and equivalent successor-system fields;
- Parentage-order and amendment processing categories;
- Parent country-of-birth fields and whose information they represent; and
- Existing parent-linkage, deduplication, plurality, or delivery-identification methods relevant to the requested counts.

Please include applicable documentation for the requested period, including documented changes in field availability or meaning.

**Format, disclosure, and costs**

Please provide responsive electronic records under Government Code § 7922.570, preferably in CSV or Excel if available in a format CDPH holds or uses. Please identify the latest date covered and label partial-year or provisional data.

If small-cell restrictions prevent release at the requested detail, I am willing to accept suppressed tables, statewide totals, or combined-year totals. Please provide the applicable suppression policy and all reasonably segregable, nonexempt portions, citing the specific legal basis for any withholding.

Before incurring any charge, including compilation, extraction, or programming charges under Government Code § 7922.575, please provide an itemized estimate and obtain my written authorization.

If responsive information is maintained differently or requires clarification, please assist me in identifying available records and practical alternatives under Government Code § 7922.600. Please produce readily available records on a rolling basis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Whiteside

communications.communication:
Thank you for contacting the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) to obtain public records. 
Your Public Records Act (PRA) request dated October 21, 2026, is being processed.  Reference Number P031528-102126 has been assigned for tracking purposes.  Please refer to this reference number for use when accessing the CDPH Public Records Center Portal to monitor the progress of your request. 
CDPH strives to answer all requests for public records in as timely a manner as possible.  Under California law, CDPH must respond to your inquiry no later than ten calendar days from receipt of the request to notify you whether records will be disclosed.   Note that some records are exempted from disclosure.  If the requested records are exempt, we will inform you in writing as to why. 
The Public Records Act (see Govt. Code §7920.000 et. seq.) provides that CDPH may extend the response period for up to 14 calendar days should it be necessary to search for records located at off-site facilities or if the request involves a voluminous amount of records.  We will notify you within 10 days of receipt of your request if a 14-day extension is necessary.  If fees are involved, CDPH will need to collect the fees before releasing the records.  However, there is typically no fee for records released electronically through the Public Records Center Portal. 
The 10- and 14-day response periods are to allow CDPH time to determine how long it will take to disclose the requested records.  Depending on the number of records requested or other factors, a response may take longer.  CDPH will do its best to provide documents on a rolling basis as they become available and to keep you informed as to the timing and type of records to be released. 
Please visit the CDPH Public Records Center Portal to monitor request progress, communicate with CDPH staff processing your request and to submit future requests. 
California Department of Public Health

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Fife Public Schools email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.

title: Potential UCSF Construction related Traffic Incidents

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Potential UCSF Construction related Traffic Incidents
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Specific to construction activities associated with the UCSF Parnassus Campus construction projects, please provide the following records:
1) A list or records identifying construction contractors and subcontractors working on hauling/delivery/movement of large vehicles at the the Parnassus Campus construction projects. This includes but not limited to general contractors, subcontractors, trucking companies, and hauling companies involved in material transport.
2) Any documents, reports, traffic plans, or logistics planning materials that estimate or describe the expected or actual volume of large construction vehicles (e.g., dump trucks, haul trucks, concrete trucks, delivery trucks) traveling to or from the Parnassus construction sites. 
3) Any internal reports, safety reviews, incident reviews, or investigations conducted by UCSF or its contractors following the pedestrian fatality involving a construction vehicle near the Parnassus construction site in approximately October 2024.
4) Any contracts, agreements, or work orders between UCSF (or its construction management entities) and Costello Trucking, including any agreements involving hauling, trucking, or material transport services connected to the Parnassus construction projects.

If records are maintained under different terminology (for example, traffic management plans, construction logistics plans, safety reviews, or contractor lists), please provide those records as well.

Request Context:
This request relates to public safety concerns surrounding large construction vehicles operating near the UCSF Parnassus construction sites. Two severe traffic incidents involving large trucks have been reported in the area, including a pedestrian fatality in October 2024. Given ongoing neighborhood concerns regarding truck traffic and pedestrian safety, this request seeks to better understand the scale of construction vehicle activity associated with the project and whether any safety reviews or mitigation measures were implemented following the 2024 incident. If any portion of this request can be clarified or narrowed to assist in locating responsive records, please feel free to contact me.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Alan J. Segal

Hello Alan Segal,


This is regarding your request for records dated April 20, 2026, made pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code, § 7920 et seq.). We have no record of an earlier request from you, so we are treating April 20, 2026 as the date of receipt.


Based on the terms of the request, the University has made a preliminary determination that the request seeks potentially disclosable records within the possession of the University. A search is being conducted and records identified as responsive to your request will be reviewed, and made available for your access, in accordance with relevant law and University policy. Please note that our collection and review are ongoing, and requested material may contain information that is exempt from disclosure under CPRA, the California Information Practices Act (CIPA), and other applicable laws and University policy.



Please also bear in mind that we are concurrently fulfilling numerous other requests, many of which were received before yours and that we generally process requests in the order in which they are received. The current timeframe for fulfillment of most requests is ten weeks, although this may vary due to the nature and complexity of the request. The current estimated response date for your request is on or by July 9, 2026.

Respectfully,



PRA Team

University of California, San Francisco

Alan

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Randolph Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Randolph Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

title: Public Records Request — Tucson Generative AI Records

communications.subject: Arizona Public Records Law Request: Public Records Request — Tucson Generative AI Records
communications.communication:
Subject: Public Records Request — AI Chatbot Interaction Logs

April 9, 2026

Public Records Officer
City of Tucson
255 W. Alameda Street
Tucson, AZ 85701

Dear Public Records Officer,

I am writing on behalf of a team of researchers and journalists from Stanford University, the University of Southern California, KNKX Public Radio and the New York Times. We are studying how government agencies are adopting and using AI tools in their daily work.

We are writing to request records related to the City of Tucson's use of generative AI tools by city employees, including Axon Draft One and generative AI tools used for permit processing.

Pursuant to the Arizona Public Records Law, A.R.S. § 39-121.01(D)(1), we are requesting the following records:

1. All interaction logs from Axon Draft One, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Claude, or any other generative AI chatbot tool — including prompts submitted by City of Tucson employees and responses generated by the AI — for the period from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed. We request these records in their native electronic format where available (e.g., HTML exports, JSON, or CSV).

2. Any policies, guidelines, acceptable use policies, or training materials governing City of Tucson employee use of Axon Draft One, generative AI permit-processing tools, or other generative AI chatbot tools.

3. Any data retention or deletion policies applicable to AI chatbot interaction logs, including any schedules for automatic deletion of interaction data.

4. Administrative usage statistics showing number of users, sessions, and queries processed for any generative AI tools deployed to city employees.

We are seeking the substantive content of AI interactions for research purposes. We do not need personally identifying information of individual employees (such as names and email addresses).

Tucson's public safety teams are piloting Axon's Draft One, which leverages generative AI and body-worn camera audio to produce draft police report narratives, with deputies reporting approximately one hour saved each day (see CNN, "How AI is being used by police departments to help draft reports," Aug. 12, 2025, https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/12/tech/ai-police-reports-axon; see also Axon, "Draft One," https://www.axon.com/products/draft-one). Administrative staff also use generative and predictive AI tools to speed up permits, translations, and data analysis. The City's Advanced Technology Committee and Technology & Data Policies require supplemental reviews, human oversight, bias checks, and director signoff before deploying AI systems (see Nucamp, "The Complete Guide to Using AI in the Government Industry in Tucson in 2025," https://www.nucamp.co/blog/coding-bootcamp-tucson-az-government-the-complete-guide-to-using-ai-in-the-government-industry-in-tucson-in-2025).

We note that records of this type have been made available in response to public records requests in other jurisdictions. See Cascade PBS, WA City Officials Are Using ChatGPT to Write Government Documents (Aug. 2025), https://www.cascadepbs.org/news/2025/08/wa-city-officials-are-using-chatgpt-to-write-government-documents/; see also Texas State AI Usage — Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT), MuckRock, https://www.muckrock.com/foi/texas-109/texas-state-ai-usage-texas-department-of-transportation-txdot-196227/#files.

The results of this research will be published in peer-reviewed academic venues and will contribute to public understanding of how public servants interact with AI systems. This request is made by an academic research institution for scholarly, non-commercial purposes; as such, we request a fee waiver or reduction. If a fee waiver is not granted, please inform me of estimated costs before proceeding. I am willing to pay fees up to $20.

I understand that this may be a novel type of records request and I am happy to answer any technical questions. Please feel free to contact me at the email address below.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,
Alexander Spangher
Postdoctoral Researcher
Stanford University
alexspan@stanford.edu

P.S. To facilitate your response, we note that Axon Draft One generates draft police reports from body-worn camera audio; the initial AI-generated drafts and any officer edits may be retained in the Axon Evidence system. For ChatGPT, conversation histories can be exported by individual users via Settings > Data Controls > Export Data. For Microsoft Copilot, interaction histories may be available through the Microsoft 365 admin console or the Purview compliance center. We are happy to provide additional technical guidance if that would be helpful.

P.P.S. Arizona's public records law requires that public bodies promptly furnish copies of public records to any person requesting them. A.R.S. § 39-121.01(D)(1). Arizona courts have broadly interpreted "public records" to include electronic communications and digital records created in the transaction of public business. Consistent with this trend nationally, NARA has made clear that chats and other electronic messages used for agency business are likely government records. NARA Bulletin 2023-02 (Jan. 5, 2023), https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/bulletins/2023/2023-02.

communications.subject: City of Tucson, AZ Public Records Request #12319
communications.communication:
October 28, 2026

Alexander Spangher
263 Huntington Ave
Boston, MA 02115

Dear Alexander Spangher:
The City of Tucson received your request under the Arizona Public Record Law, A.R.S 39-121 on May 6, 2026.  The City has searched for responsive records and responds as follows.
Request 1: Interaction logs (prompts and responses) from generative AIT tools, January 1, 2025 to present.
The City’s search has found the following:

  *
ChatGPT Teams/Claude Teams: The City’s administrator can export usage logs only from July 1, 2026 forward. Those logs contain usage metadata, meaning account activity and token consumption. They do not contain the text of user prompts or AI-generated responses. The City has no prompt-level or response-level content for these platforms for any period, and it has no logs of any kind for January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. The Public Records Law does not require a public body to create records that do not exist.
  *   Axon Draft One: The City does not use this platform and therefore has no responsive records.
  *   Generative AI Permit-Processing tools (Alynea/IDA): The City does not use and therefore has no responsive records.
  *   Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, and any other generative AI chatbot: The City has not yet deployed this tool and therefore has no responsive records.

Request 2: Policies, guidelines, acceptable use policies, and training materials.
The City’s applicable directive is Administrative Directive AD 1.08-8, Artificial Intelligence Policy, which is publicly available:
https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/tucson/latest/tucson_az_admin/1_08_8__artificial__intelligence__policy. The City’s AI Training Completion Dashboard reflects completion of AI training by 916 employees. It reports completion status and is not a training-materials record.
Request 3: Data retention and deletion policies for AI chatbot interaction logs.
The City has no AI-specific records retention policy and no schedule for automatic deletion of AI interaction data. The City’s Records Management program determines the applicable retention period under the City’s general retention schedules and the state schedules adopted under A.R.S. § 41-151.12].
Request 4: Administrative usage statistics (users, sessions, queries).
The City does not track session-level or query-level data, and the platforms available to it do not provide that information to the City. As noted under Request 1, the only usage data the City can export is account-level metadata from July 1, 2026 forward, which includes token consumption. The AI Training Completion Dashboard reports training completion and not tool usage. The City has no other responsive records.



Thank you,

Dawna Howard

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: ALPR Contract Terms, Licensed Products, Funding, and Data Deletion
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records held by City Of Richardson related to agreements with any automated license plate reader (ALPR) or surveillance technology vendor (for example Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions, or Axon), from the start of the first such agreement to present:

1. All contracts, master service agreements, order forms, quotes, amendments, renewals, and terms of service, including any terms addressing data ownership, the vendor's rights to use, aggregate, or share data, data retention, data disposition upon termination, automatic renewal, termination, and price changes.
2. Records identifying every vendor product, feature, or service licensed or enabled, including but not limited to license plate readers, video cameras, drones, gunshot detection, investigative or AI-assisted search tools, and integrations with third-party camera networks.
3. Records showing the current contract term, expiration or renewal date, and the projected cost of renewal.
4. Grant applications, award letters, and grant agreements used to fund ALPR or related technology, including any conditions on use and the grant period.
5. Any notices received since August 1, 2026 from the Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, any other state agency, or any vendor regarding suspension of grant funding, payment pauses, contract changes, or removal of cameras.
6. Any certifications, attestations, or written confirmations from the vendor regarding deletion of data in accordance with the contract or the agency's retention policy.
7. Any vendor-provided usage, effectiveness, or return-on-investment reports.

This request covers records held by any city department, including the Richardson Police Department, as well as the City Secretary's Office, Purchasing, and Finance.

Please release all non-exempt portions and cite the specific statutory exception for anything withheld. If any item is unclear, please contact me for clarification rather than denying it.

I request records in their existing electronic format (such as native exports, CSV, or PDF) delivered by email or download link. I do not request paper copies, printouts, or physical media such as CDs or flash drives. I am not requesting that new reports be created. Please do not refer me to an online transparency portal in place of producing these records.

I request a waiver or reduction of fees, as release of this information primarily benefits the general public by informing residents about the use of surveillance technology in their community. If charges will exceed $40, please provide an itemized estimate, including any less costly alternative, before work begins.

Thank you for your cooperation. I look forward to your prompt response, as required by the Texas Public Information Act.

Sincerely,
Blackland Prairie Records Project

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Consumer complaints regarding Freecash / Almedia (2020–present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the following records:

All consumer complaints received by the FTC or held in the Consumer Sentinel Network that name, or describe in their text, any of the following:
- Freecash
- Freecash.com
- Free Cash app
- FreeSkins / freeskins.com
- Almedia GmbH
- Almedia USA, Inc.
- Almedia Ops UK Ltd
- Almedia Online LLC
- 256 Rewards Ltd

Include complaints contributed by other organizations (such as the Better Business Bureau and state attorneys general) to the extent the FTC can release them. Include Do Not Call and unwanted text-message complaints.

If the full complaints cannot be released, a count of those complaints by year and by complaint category, with reported dollar losses where recorded.

Date range: 1 January 2020 to present.

I prefer the records as a spreadsheet (CSV or Excel) of complaint fields and narrative text.

I request a fee waiver under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii). The records concern a widely used US consumer app's practices: earnings claims, withheld payouts and unsolicited text messages. Disclosure will add significantly to public understanding of how these practices affect consumers. I have no commercial interest in the records.

If any part of this request is denied, please release the rest that is not exempt and cite the specific exemption for each part withheld.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Yax Falk

All or part of your request seeks consumer complaint records. These records are maintained and retrieved from the FTC's Consumer Sentinel Network (CSN) database. When the results of a CSN search exceeds 200 consumer complaints, the time and effort required to redact personally identifiable information is unreasonably burdensome. CSN complaints contain both free-form (i.e. no limit on the type of information that can be entered), and non-free form fields (i.e. the type of information that is limited by pre-set options). Free form fields may contain personally identifiable information (e.g. complainant name, address, email, etc.). This information is automatically redacted. The fields that don't seek personally identifiable information must be "manually" reviewed. This is necessary because, even when the field itself doesn't ask for personally identifiable information, consumers routinely insert personally identifiable information that the FTC must redact. Therefore, the FTC limits production of CSN results to a sample of 200 complaints.

In addition to the 200-complaint sample, we could produce a limited set of bulk data for the balance of the search results. This bulk data would consist only of the non-free form fields (e.g. complaint date, consumer and company state, consumer age range and military status, complaint info topic). If you are interested in receiving this limited data set, you must let us know within 3 business days. Otherwise, we will only respond with the 200-sample set. For future requests that you submit for consumer complaint data, please indicate in your initial request whether request whether you are seeking the bulk data.

As soon as we are able, an individual FTC employee will reach out to let you know that they are starting work on your request and will provide their contact information.

In the meantime, if you have questions or concerns, please reach out to us at foia@ftc.gov<mailto:foia@ftc.gov>. If you should have any questions regarding your request, please contact us at foia@ftc.gov<mailto:foia@ftc.gov>. In any call or future correspondence concerning the request, please refer to the following case number FOIA-2027-00023.
Best,
FTC FOIA Team

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: DoD/Dept. of War support for "The Promotion of General Davis"
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents pertaining to collaboration between the Department of Defense (DoD)/Dept. of War and the production of "The Promotion of General Davis." This title appears on a list of 2025 DoD/Dept. of War entertainment industry collaborations released to me through FOIA. The list is attached to this request. Requested documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; photographs; and all records of communications between employees of DoD/Dept. of War and members of the cast, crew, and production company of "The Promotion of General Davis," including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation as well as the editor-in-chief and a contributor to a research magazine published by said foundation titled "Cultural Engineering Studies." These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

title: Sacramento Sheriffs Office Shoot Of Ingold Guttenbeil

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Sacramento Sheriffs Office Shoot Of Ingold Guttenbeil
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A. The October 4, 2026 shooting (Pen. Code § 832.7(b)(1)(A)(i))

This incident involved the discharge of firearms at a person by peace officers, so all records listed in § 832.7(b)(2) are subject to disclosure, including:

All investigative reports, including incident, supplemental, and use-of-force reports.
All photographic, audio, and video evidence, including body-worn camera, dash/in-car camera, surveillance or business video collected from the car wash or neighboring businesses, and any bystander video the Office obtained.
All 911 call audio, dispatch radio audio, and CAD records for the call that prompted the response.
Transcripts or recordings of interviews with deputies, witnesses, and the reporting party.
The autopsy report and any coroner's records in the Office's possession.
All materials compiled and presented to the District Attorney or any other body charged with determining whether to file charges, or whether the deputies' conduct complied with law and policy.
All documents setting forth findings or recommended findings, and any disciplinary records relating to the incident.
The names, badge numbers, and assignments of the three deputies who fired. Officer names are not confidential. (Commission on Peace Officer Standards & Training v. Superior Court (2007) 42 Cal.4th 278.)
Records identifying the firearm the Office reports recovering, its location when found, and any evidence-collection or chain-of-custody records documenting where it was found.

B. Critical incident video (Gov. Code § 7923.625)

Separately from Part A, I request all video and audio recordings of this critical incident. The Office has stated publicly that it intends to release body-worn camera footage. If release is delayed, please state the specific basis for the delay in writing, as the statute requires.

C. Related incidents involving Mr. Guttenbeil (Gov. Code §§ 7923.610, 7923.615)

The Office has publicly linked Mr. Guttenbeil to two prior incidents. I request the information the statute requires to be disclosed for:

The alleged shooting at the Marconi/Eastern intersection on the night of October 3, 2026: time, date, and location; time and date of report; factual circumstances; description of any injuries, property, or weapons involved; and CAD records.
The June 2026 arrest at the same intersection for suspected assault with a deadly weapon: arrestee information, factual circumstances of the arrest, charges, and the disposition.

D. Prior records of the involved deputies (Pen. Code § 832.7(b)(1))

For each of the three deputies who fired, all records of any other incident involving:
the discharge of a firearm at a person;
use of force resulting in death or great bodily injury;
a sustained finding of unreasonable or excessive force;
failure to intervene;
dishonesty;
unlawful arrest or search;
prejudice or discrimination.

E. Policies

The Office's use-of-force policy, de-escalation policy, body-worn camera policy, and critical-incident video release policy in effect on October 4, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson
