title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Milford Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Milford Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: RE: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Milford Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Joshua Dankoff,

With respect to request #1, the Milford Police Department does not have policies per se regarding communication and information sharing between department employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. All officers have been made aware of the Protect Act, and we rely on that regarding immigration issues.

With respect to request #2, the Milford Police Department does not have any policies concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. Once again, we rely on the provisions of the Protect Act.

Request #3 is attached. Please note that the report cited in the email (26-22136-AR) is a DOMESTIC report and is not a public record in accordance with M.G.L. c. 4 s. 7 cl. 26 (A).

Sincerely,


John Sanchioni
   Deputy Chief

milfordpolice.org
508-473-1113 x3621
sanchioni@milfordpolice.org<mailto:sanchioni@milfordpolice.org>

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Hagerstown Police Department)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Hagerstown Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Hagerstown Police Department.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Hagerstown Police Department. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Hagerstown Police Department, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Hagerstown Police Department data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Hagerstown Police Department policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Hagerstown Police Department audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Hagerstown Police Department personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Hagerstown Police Department.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Hagerstown Police Department.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Hagerstown Police Department or by third party who make the information available to Hagerstown Police Department. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Hagerstown Police Department’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. Alternatively, please consider waiving any fees, pursuant to § 4-206(e)(2)(ii) of the General Provisions Article, as this request is on behalf of individuals served by the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, a state government agency, which solely serves indigent citizens of Maryland. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Gilleran
Chief Attorney
Forensics Division
Office of the Public Defender
6 St. Paul St., Suite 1508
Baltimore, MD 21202
(410) 804-7107
jeffrey.gilleran@maryland.gov

William Beckett

title: Costa Mesa Police drone flights, DFR pilot and Skydio-Axon purchase

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Costa Mesa Police drone flights, DFR pilot and Skydio-Axon purchase
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records concerning the Costa Mesa Police Department’s unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and Drone as First Responder (DFR) program, including:

1. Flight and deployment logs for April 18, 2025, through October 6, 2026, including the reported 459 deployments in fiscal year 2025–26 and DFR operations at South Coast Plaza. Please include available dates and times, general locations, call-for-service or incident identifiers, flight duration, outcomes, and any records showing who accessed or viewed recorded footage.

2. Records evaluating the three-week DFR pilot conducted with Skydio Inc. in May and June 2025, including the evaluation, operational data, pilot plans, reports, and communications about results or recommendations.

3. Records concerning the City Council’s October 6, 2026, approval of a two-year purchase from Axon Enterprise Inc. (Skydio Inc.) under Omnia Contract No. 3544-21-4615, including the purchase agreement and amendments, quote 834688-004, statement of work, purchase orders, invoices, grant-funding records, and implementation plans for the Skydio X-10 drone and three docking stations.

4. Current CMPD Policy 606 and records governing DFR deployment, footage retention, access, sharing, public disclosure, and audit logs for footage stored in Axon Evidence.

Please search records held by Capt. Carlos Diaz, Lt. Nick Wilson, the Police Department personnel responsible for UAS operations and procurement, and the City Clerk/City Manager’s offices, including communications with Axon Enterprise Inc. or Skydio Inc. from May 1, 2025, through October 6, 2026, concerning the pilot, DFR operations, data or footage, and the approved purchase.

Source: https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/news/story/2026-10-07/as-costa-mesa-mulls-surveillance-privacy-police-expand-drone-force

Please waive any fees, as these records will be used in the course of reporting for 404media.co.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Koebler

title: Gang Unit Policies & Database Records

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Gang Unit Policies & Database Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

1. Policies and General Orders: All current department policies, general orders, standard operating procedures (SOPs), special orders, training manuals, or memoranda governing the Aurora Police Department's identification, documentation, tracking, and validation of individuals as suspected gang members, associates, or affiliates.
2. Criteria Guidelines: Any documents detailing the explicit threshold criteria used by APD officers or specialized units (e.g., Gang Unit, Special Operations Group) to determine whether an individual is entered into a gang database or designated as gang-affiliated (including criteria regarding tattoos, clothing, associates, social media, or self-admission).
3. Database Specifications: Records detailing the name, architecture, vendor, and system parameters of any local database, software platform, or intelligence system utilized by APD to store gang affiliation data.
4. Data Sharing & Interoperability: All agreements, memorandums of understanding (MOUs), or policy documents detailing how APD shares or receives gang-related data with outside entities (e.g., county sheriff's offices, Illinois State Police, federal agencies, or regional multi-jurisdictional intelligence centers).
5. Auditing, Oversight, and Removal: Any policies, guidelines, or logs concerning the periodic review, auditing, purging, or removal of individuals' names from APD or shared gang databases, including any provisions allowing individuals to contest or appeal their designation.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

M

communications.communication:
Dear Elizabeth Evans-Ralston: 
Thank you for your interest in public records of Massachusetts Department of Correction. Your request has been received and is being processed in accordance with the Public Information Act. Your request was received in this office on 10/25/2026 and given the reference number R001330-102526 for tracking purposes. Records Requested: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records: 

All available contracting and procurement documents and communications, including requests for proposals (RFPs) and/or requests for quotes (RFQs); all bids and proposals; all executed contracts with amendments, extensions, and supportive materials (active and expired); and any related agreements between Massachusetts Department of Corrections and/or Massachusetts State Government and private healthcare contracting corporations that were active or published between January 1, 2001 and December 31, 2025. This includes any documents related to contracts from before 2001, but active during the period of interest. 

To assist in your search, below is a partial list of documents that we believe should be included in this request: 

- RFR #24-DOC-9004-Prison Health Services 
- RFR #19-DOC-9004-Prison Health Services 

If healthcare operations for incarcerated individuals in Massachusetts State Prisons were contracted to entities other than private healthcare contracting corporations (ex. Universities), we request the same available documents during active or published between January 1, 2001 and December 31, 2025. 

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage. 

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Elizabeth Evans-Ralston

You can monitor the progress of your request at the link below and you'll receive an email when your request has been completed. Again, thank you for using the MADOC Public Records Request Center. 
Massachusetts Department of Correction

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Stanely Sporkin (Federal Bureau of Investigation)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Stanley Sporkin (February 7, 1932 – March 23, 2020), who was a director of enforcement for the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), general counsel for the Central Intelligence Agency and United States federal judge of the United States District Court for the District of Columbia. This request includes, but is not limited to, any internally produced history studies which deal with Mr. Sporkin and his time as general counsel.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma Best

Thank you for contacting foipaquestions@fbi.gov.  Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on “Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request” on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request
If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-0] please enter [1234567-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-1] please enter [1234567-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@fbi.gov.

FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly

Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]

FOIPA:
Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:
FOIPA:
1234567-000

Case Type:
FOIPA

Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)
The FBI’s FOIPA Program is searching the FBI’s indices for potentially responsive documents.
You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 106 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 785 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 1,695 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 2,088 days for processing.

Respectfully,


Public Information Officer

Winchester, VA  22602

Note:  This is a non-emergency email address.  If this is an emergency, please call 911 directly.  If you need to report a tip for immediate action, please contact FBI Tips at http://tips.fbi.gov/ or reach out to your local field office.

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Fall River Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Fall River Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

Pursuant to the Nebraska Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Missouri Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Missouri Sunshine Law (RSMo Chapter 610), I request copies of the following public records. The date range for this request is August 1, 2026 through September 30, 2026, except for contract and payment records under item 3, which run from each contract's start through September 30, 2026.

In this request, a reference to any record includes that record under any title the District uses for it; where a title differs, I request the record that serves that function.

1. The complete agenda packet (including all attachments) for the September 23, 2026 Business / Tax Rate Hearing (Regular Business Meeting), specifically the contract action report / board action summary for agenda item 027-S-009-103: RSP & Associates, LLC — $83,100.
2. The complete agenda packet (including all attachments) for the August 26, 2026 Regular Business Meeting, specifically any contract action report / board action summary for Education Partners Practice & Policy — $102,000.

For each item, the request covers: scope of work / statement of work, funding source, contract term and dates, the approved amount, and the vote/approval record.

3. For each of the two contracts above, the executed contract (also called the agreement or professional services agreement), plus all amendments or change orders, and line-item invoices submitted and payments (also called payment records or disbursement records) made, through September 30, 2026.
4. If either contract resulted from a competitive solicitation, the solicitation document and any evaluation or scoring summary (also called a scoring matrix or evaluation summary).

Please provide records in electronic format where available, and produce records on a rolling basis as they are located and reviewed rather than holding all records until the full set is complete. If any portion is withheld or redacted, please cite the specific statutory exemption and release all reasonably segregable portions. If search or duplication fees are expected to exceed $50, please contact me with an estimate before processing; I do not authorize fees above $50 without my prior written approval.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Felipe Acano

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Franklin Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Franklin Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)
